We have evidence:
- Source 1: Tyr4a, Tyr4b, Cas9 RNAs introduced. Tail-DNA analysis identified multiple mutant alleles in completely albino hybrid founder #30. Authors attribute within-founder diversity to mosaicism, potentially arising from editing persisted into cleavage stages. Deep sequencing reported 57 mutant alleles threshold across 23 hybrid founders; not 57 injected animals.
- Source 2: C57BL/6N mosaics produced albino progeny in crosses with albino mates. Hybrid pigmentation mosaics were not tested this way: they already carried the FVB/NJ albino allele, which could produce albino offspring without demonstrating transmission of a newly induced allele. Somatic evidence and C57 crosses do not establish new-allele transmission for untested hybrids.

one_founder_per_allele: each allele from different injected animal; identifier combines founders.
other: substantive answer outside alternatives.
uniform_one_allele_pair: all sampled cells can be represented by one common pair of Tyr alleles; albinism establishes uniform mutant genotype.
within_founder_mosaicism: Different mutant alleles occur within same founder, so complete albinism does not establish one uniform mutant genotype.
